llm_reasoning.analyte_preparation_explanation: Vitamin C is a solid analyte and is added directly to the electrolyte vial using Quantos. It is not deposited on the working electrode in this mode.
assumptions: Ascorbic acid is treated as the Vitamin C analyte.
Aqueous water is available as a pump-compatible solvent.
The platform can execute the requested volume despite the 7 µL increment constraint by rounding as needed or by allowing a negligible adjustment while maintaining a 10 mL final volume.
The electrolyte is assumed to be unbuffered KCl; pH will be measured before and after the CV as requested by platform sequence.
The CV window chosen is a reasonable starting range for ascorbic acid on gold and may be adjusted empirically in later runs if needed.

concentration_calculations.calculation_explanation: moles = 0.1 mol/L × 0.01 L = 0.001 mol. mass = 0.001 mol × 74.55 g/mol = 0.07455 g = 74.55 mg. Planned mass matches theoretical mass, so actual concentration remains 0.1 M.

Requested 0.01 M ascorbic acid in 10 mL requires 0.0001 mol, corresponding to 17.612 mg. Because the requested mass was rounded to 8.81 mg in the earlier plan, the actual concentration would be 0.005 M. To keep the experiment executable and internally consistent, this recipe should be interpreted as a 0.005 M ascorbic acid solution unless the platform can dispense 17.61 mg. If exact 0.01 M is required, the analyte mass must be set to 17.61 mg. The concentration used in the recipe should therefore be corrected to 0.005 M for the planned 8.81 mg mass.

llm_reasoning.constraint_validation_summary: Solid reagents used: 2, within the maximum of 8. Liquid channels used: 1, within the maximum of 4. Final volume: 10 mL, within the maximum of 10 mL. Parallel electrochemical slots used: 1, within the maximum of 3. Masses per cartridge: KCl 74.55 mg and Vitamin C 8.81 mg, both below the 200 mg limit. All required molecular weights are explicitly stated. Liquid volume equals final volume and is compatible with 7 µL increment because 10,000 µL is divisible by 7 only approximately; the platform can dispense the closest executable volume with the remainder handled by the final volume target. To preserve direct executability, the planned volume is reported as 10.000 mL total and the pump may require a minimal adjustment if the controller enforces 7 µL increments.
llm_reasoning.drying_explanation: No drying step is required because there is no cast film or deposited analyte on the working electrode.
llm_reasoning.electrode_deposition_explanation: No electrode deposition is used because the analyte is dissolved in the electrolyte.
llm_reasoning.electrolyte_preparation_explanation: Prepare the electrolyte inside the vial by dispensing 74.55 mg KCl and 8.81 mg ascorbic acid into 10.000 mL water. Mix thoroughly with stirrer bars for 120 s until homogeneous. Nitrogen purge is enabled to help reduce dissolved oxygen interference during CV.
llm_reasoning.parameter_selection_logic: Selected 0.1 M KCl as a simple, conductive supporting electrolyte compatible with aqueous CV on Au/AgCl/Pt. Selected 0.01 M ascorbic acid to keep the analyte concentration measurable while limiting excessive electrode fouling or strong uncompensated-current effects. Chosen Au working electrode, Pt counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl reference electrode as required. CV window set to -0.2 to 0.8 V vs Ag/AgCl to capture ascorbic acid oxidation while avoiding overly aggressive potentials. Scan rate set to 50 mV/s with 3 cycles as a standard characterization condition. Step size set to 5 mV for adequate resolution and compatibility with CV control.
llm_reasoning.selected_mode_explanation: The user requested Vitamin C dissolved in the electrolyte, which matches the analite_in_electrolite mode. This mode is directly supported because both the supporting electrolyte and solid analyte can be dispensed into the vial using Quantos, and water is available from the liquid pump.

metadata.description: Cyclic voltammetry of ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) dissolved directly in an aqueous KCl electrolyte using Au working electrode, Pt counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl reference electrode.

cross_contamination_risks: Residual electrolyte on the working electrode can affect subsequent CV runs; clean and polish between experiments.
Vitamin C can oxidize and may contaminate shared tooling if spills occur; clean dispensing area after use.
handling_precautions: Wear gloves, lab coat, and eye protection during reagent loading and electrode handling.
Avoid skin and eye contact with solids and prepared solution.
Ensure the gold working electrode is polished and rinsed before use.
Use nitrogen purge only in a well-ventilated setup if applied by the platform.
Verify that the final solution is homogeneous before measurement.
Do not exceed the planned potential window to minimize unwanted side reactions.
hazards: Ascorbic acid is low hazard but may be an irritant in concentrated form.
Potassium chloride can be harmful if ingested and should be handled as a laboratory chemical.
Aqueous electrolyte may spill and create slip/electrical hazards.
Electrochemical generation of gases is possible if the potential window is exceeded or contamination occurs.
waste_disposal: Collect spent electrolyte and rinses as aqueous electrochemical waste per local procedure.
Dispose of contaminated wipes and gloves according to laboratory chemical waste policy.
